The debut arrives for a club in a rough spot. Philadelphia is 1-6-3 with 5 points through 10 games, and the early numbers say the record is not just bad luck. The Flyers have generated 38.3% of the expected goals (a measure of chance quality, with 50% meaning an even fight) so far this season, and at five-on-five that drops to 34%. They are being outplayed, not just outscored. Their goals are also 8.5 below what their shots should have produced, so finishing has hurt them, but goaltending has not: the team's goalies have saved 3.3 goals more than expected. Special teams give little cover, with the power play creating 0.62 expected goals per game and the penalty kill allowing 0.69. For a young player stepping in, the open question is whether he can help a team that is short on quality chances, which no single debut will fix on its own.

In other words, Rust's absence may cost the Penguins less production than his scoring line implies. His 29 goals last season show he's a real scorer, though, and some regression was likely anyway.

The bigger concern is the team. Pittsburgh is 3-5-1 with a 49.3 percent share of expected goals overall, and its five-on-five share is a healthier 55 percent. The Penguins are 3 goals below expected, so the record may be worse than the play. Losing a forward now, though, makes a rebound harder.

stories.take:
The Athletic reports that the Ducks signed defenseman Tristan Luneau to a six-year, $43.2 million contract extension despite his having played only 14 career NHL games.

The early numbers are decent but not yet a justification. So far this season, Luneau has played 21.89 minutes a game across six games, with no goals and one assist. His own expected goals are 0.31, so he is 0.31 below that mark, which is a tiny gap on a tiny sample. At 5-on-5, the Ducks hold 50.4 percent of the expected goals with him on the ice, and the team is 5.5 percentage points better with him out there than without him. That is a real positive on a club that sits at 46 percent at 5-on-5 and 48.6 percent overall, though Anaheim's 4-2-0 record leans on goals saved above expected (+2.8) and scoring 1.3 above expected, not on controlling play. The big minutes show the coaching staff already trusts him, but six games cannot confirm the contract. The deal is a bet on what he becomes, and his early on-ice impact is the first modest evidence for it.

stories.take:
The Athletic reports that its contract grades have the Red Wings locking down Alex DeBrincat at a fair rate for a top scorer, noting he has scored 111 goals in 252 games with Detroit.

The numbers so far this season back up the "top scorer" label without suggesting he is running hot. DeBrincat has 5 goals and 9 points in 8 games, against 4.1 expected goals (a measure of the quality of his chances), so he is only 0.9 goals above what his shots would normally produce. That is a small gap, which says his production is mostly real. He is also driving play: DET controls 57 percent of the expected goals at 5-on-5 when he is on the ice, and the team's share of the chances is about 8 percentage points better with him than without him. For a Detroit team sitting at 3-3-2 with a 49.8 percent expected goals share overall, that matters. The Red Wings have been outscored by 7.6 goals relative to their chances, so DeBrincat is one of the clearer reasons the underlying results look better than the record.

The team was 2.5 percentage points better with him off it. The Canadiens drop a defenseman who played 59 games last season (2 goals, 12 points) and gain the pick.

moves.take: Per the Oilers' announcement, Edmonton acquired center Filip Hallander from Pittsburgh in exchange for defenseman Spencer Stastney. Hallander has 3 points in 5 games this season and owns a 64.99 five-on-five share of expected goals, with Pittsburgh's share 14.35 points better when he plays. Stastney, who played 66 games for Edmonton last year, has just two games with the Penguins and no points. Edmonton arrives at 5-1-1 with a 52 percent five-on-five share, so Hallander joins a team already controlling chances.
